query_logs.title: Run a KQL query against the workspace
query_logs.description:
Execute a Kusto query against the connected Log Analytics workspace and return its tables. This is the tool this connector exists for.
Always pass `timespan`. Without it the query runs against every day of retained data, which on a real workspace is slow, expensive and usually hits a limit rather than returning. `PT1H` is the last hour, `P7D` the last week, and `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z/2026-01-02T00:00:00Z` an explicit window.
Use `| summarize` and `| take` in the query rather than pulling raw rows out: the service caps a response at roughly 500,000 rows and 100 MB, and aggregating in KQL is far cheaper than aggregating afterwards.
`additional_workspaces` runs the same query across other workspaces as well, addressed by workspace id, resource id or name.
The result is in `tables[0]`, as `columns` and positional `rows`.
query_logs.notes: Omitting timespan scans all retained data. Results are capped at about 500,000 rows and 100 MB.

query.description: The KQL query. Table names are case-sensitive; get_metadata lists the tables this workspace actually has.

timespan.description: The window to query, as an ISO 8601 duration (PT1H, P7D) or a start/end pair separated by a slash. Omitting it scans everything retained.

additional_workspaces.description: Other workspaces to include in the query, by workspace id, ARM resource id or name. The connected workspace is always included.

prefer.description: Server hints, most usefully a longer timeout: "wait=600" raises the query timeout to 600 seconds, and "include-statistics=true" adds execution statistics to the response.

output.description: The query result as tables of columns and positional rows.

tables.description: Each with name, columns (name and type) and rows (positional lists). tables[0] is the query's own result.

error.description: Present when the query failed; carries code, message and details.

statistics.description: Execution statistics, when include-statistics was requested via Prefer.

query_logs_get.title: Run a short KQL query via the query string
query_logs_get.description:
The same query, sent as URL parameters instead of a JSON body. Equivalent to query_logs and subject to the same limits, but bounded by URL length, so it only suits short queries.
Worth having because it is the form most Azure CLI and PowerShell examples use, which makes a query copied from documentation easier to reproduce exactly. Prefer query_logs for anything longer than a line.
query_logs_get.notes: Bounded by URL length. Use query_logs for anything but a short query.

query.description: The KQL query. Keep it short -- it goes in the URL.

timespan.description: The window to query, as an ISO 8601 duration or a start/end pair.

output.description: The query result as tables of columns and positional rows.

tables.description: Each with name, columns and rows.

get_metadata.title: List the tables, functions and solutions in the workspace
get_metadata.description:
Everything the workspace knows about itself: the tables it holds with their columns and types, the saved functions available to queries, the solutions installed, the resources sending data, and the categories those tables fall into.
This is the tool to call before writing a query against an unfamiliar workspace. Log Analytics table names are case-sensitive and vary by which data sources are configured -- `ContainerLogV2` exists only where Container Insights is on, `SigninLogs` only where Entra ID diagnostics are exported -- so guessing a table name is how most queries fail.

output.description: The workspace's schema and everything queryable in it.

tables.description: Each table with its name, columns (name and type), description and the solutions it belongs to.

functions.description: Saved functions, each with its name, body and parameters.

solutions.description: Installed monitoring solutions and the tables each contributes.

resources.description: Azure resources sending data to this workspace.

categories.description: The categories the tables are grouped under in the portal.

query_logs_batch.title: Run several KQL queries in one request
query_logs_batch.description:
Submit up to 100 queries in a single call and get all their results back together, each identified by the `id` you gave it. Much faster than issuing them one at a time when building a dashboard or a report, because it costs one round trip instead of one per query.
Each entry in `requests` is `{"id": "1", "workspace": "<workspace-id>", "body": {"query": "...", "timespan": "PT1H"}}`. The `workspace` field is required on every entry even when it is the connected workspace.
Responses come back in `responses`, in no guaranteed order, each with its `id` and either a `body` holding tables or an error. One query failing does not fail the batch, so check each response.
query_logs_batch.notes: Up to 100 queries per batch. A failure in one query does not fail the others -- check each response.

requests.description: The queries, each {"id": "1", "workspace": "<workspace-id>", "body": {"query": "...", "timespan": "PT1H"}}. Up to 100 entries.

output.description: One response per query, keyed by the id you supplied.

responses.description: Each with id, status and either body.tables or an error object.
